topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the lecture in the context of the broader cancer series, and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer Biology and Sources of Mutation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and introduce the intrinsic and extrinsic processes that generate somatic mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and the 'Bad Luck' Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine environmental carcinogen exposures and evaluate the epidemiological evidence and scientific debate surrounding intrinsic 'bad luck' versus preventable causation.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, focusing in detail on the discovery and molecular etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagenesis by Chemical and Physical Agents
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how chemical mutagens and radiation damage DNA, emphasizing how host metabolic processes can activate inert compounds into reactive carcinogens.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility cooperate with initiating mutations to facilitate malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Evaluating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the complementary genomic, observational, and experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Balance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing cancer risk as a practical benefit-risk balance and summarizing the main takeaways.
